result.title: Classical structural priors improve neural molecular representations in molecule language models
result.comment: 40 pages. This is the originally submitted version. The final version, revised after peer review, is published in J. Chem. Inf. Model. (2026): https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.6c02225
result.summary: Classical molecular similarity is central to chemical information systems, yet molecule-language models trained on paired structure-text data do not necessarily organize molecular embeddings according to graded structural relationships. Here we introduce Structure-Aware Guided Alignment (SAGA), a training-only regularizer that uses Centered Kernel Alignment to align neural molecular representations with fingerprint-based Tanimoto similarity, without adding parameters or requiring fingerprints at inference. In MolCA and Atomas, SAGA improves molecule-text retrieval, shifts non-exact retrieval toward closer structural analogues, and increases average scaffold-split property-prediction performance, while molecular description and text-to-molecule generation are improved or preserved in single-run ablations. These results show that established chemoinformatics priors can make molecule-language representations more chemically faithful while retaining their multimodal utility.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SAGA，一种仅训练期使用的正则项，用 Centered Kernel Alignment 把分子语言模型（MolCA、Atomas）的内部表示对齐到指纹 Tanimoto 相似度，在不增加参数、推理时也无需指纹的前提下改善检索与 scaffold 划分的性质预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用外部相似度结构约束内部表示几何、且不增加推理开销」的训练式对齐思路，可供核查是否能用于向 VLM latent 状态注入结构或视觉先验，并作为表示保真度的诊断线索；但与视觉推理主线无直接关联，迁移属推测。
